strengths: Well-motivated combination of multi-scale priors with speculative decoding that effectively leverages spatial locality insights
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple metrics (GenEval, DPG-Bench, FID, HPSv2) and extensive ablation studies validating each component
Clear, well-written presentation with effective visualizations and thorough supplementary material including algorithm descriptions and implementation details
Principled technical design with proper formulation of relaxed acceptance criteria, well-defined local expansion mechanism, and explicit latency analysis
Addresses practical constraints including KV-cache efficiency and integration with next-token prediction MLLMs without architecture retraining
weaknesses: Modest speedup improvements (1.22-1.68×) represent only 10-20% relative gains over LANTERN baseline, with practical significance questionable given added complexity
Non-negligible quality degradation at aggressive speedup settings: 0.8-1.7 point GenEval drops and 1.1 point HPSv2 drop at 1024p, undermining the efficiency-fidelity tradeoff
Limited evaluation scope restricted to single model (Tar-1.5B) and dataset (MS-COCO 5k); generalizability to other AR architectures, datasets, and resolution pairs remains undemonstrated

Problematic baseline comparison: LANTERN achieves 1.75-1.82× on LlamaGen but only 1.08-1.42× on Tar; Tar's much higher GenEval (77.7% vs 32%) and LANTERN drafter's low Top-1 accuracy (0.12-0.22 vs 0.38) undermine confidence in baseline fairness

Architectural constraint fundamentally limits speedup: drafter shares computational complexity with target model, speedup derived only from reduced NFE with 3-5% overhead; bottleneck appears in 2× case (Figure 7)

Limited technical novelty: multi-scale AR, local verification, and relaxed acceptance criteria are all established techniques; primary contribution is compositional rather than introducing fundamental new insights
Acceptance threshold τ lacks principled selection methodology and introduces hyperparameter sensitivity; sweeping to match LANTERN's GenEval may bias comparison unfairly
Local expansion radius l (set to 3) acknowledged as resolution-dependent but ablated only at 512p due to computational constraints; generalization methodology unclear
Probability pooling component provides marginal gains (Figure 5b) with unclear necessity relative to added complexity

strengths: Well-motivated combination of multi-scale drafting and local verification that effectively exploits spatial structure of images
Strong empirical results with up to 5× speedup at 1024p while preserving semantic alignment (GenEval degradation ≤0.2%)
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple model sizes, resolutions, and metrics with extensive ablation studies (Figures 5, 9)
Excellent presentation with clear visualizations and thorough implementation details enabling reproducibility
Practical compatibility with next-token prediction MLLMs without requiring custom sampling schedules
Detailed latency analysis (Figure 7) demonstrating overhead is only 3-5% and showing benefits of parallel decoding integration
weaknesses: Incremental novelty: individual components (multi-scale drafting, local verification, parallel decoding) are straightforward extensions of existing ideas; primary contribution is engineering-focused

Significant architectural constraints undermining practical utility: requires maintaining two model checkpoints with duplicate weights and KV-caches, creating memory overhead acknowledged as 'prohibitive on memory-constrained devices' without proposed solution

Quality-efficiency trade-off inadequately addressed: FID degradation of ~8% relative at 1024p (37.9→34.8) and consistent HPSv2 drops (0.3-1.0 points) contradict claims of maintaining 'comparable quality'; should be more prominently discussed

Unfair baseline comparisons: (1) LANTERN drafter achieves only 0.12 Top-1 accuracy on Tar vs 0.38 on LlamaGen despite identical training, raising questions about implementation fairness; (2) ZipAR achieves 3.65× speedup without quality loss—MULO-SD's ~1.5× advantage over ZipAR comes partially from accepting lower quality

Limited evaluation scope: only two model families (Tar, LlamaGen) and single dataset (MS-COCO); no evaluation on other AR models mentioned in related work (VAR, M-VAR, Switti, etc.); generalization unclear

Method complexity with underspecified design choices: multiple interdependent hyperparameters (τ, k, δ, l); local expansion radius shown resolution-dependent but no principled selection strategy; explanation of why both probability pooling and τ needed when they serve similar roles

Incomplete technical justification: claim that different rejection islands can be resampled concurrently with accepted tokens as 'sufficient context' lacks formal justification given autoregressive dependencies; theoretical speedup formula (Eq. 10) is elementary with no analysis of when local expansion helps/hurts

Training overhead not characterized: upsampler training requires 300k steps on large dataset (20M-30M parameters) but computational cost unreported; pixel-space variant training-free but with higher FLOPs (VQ decode→upsample→encode)

Presentation issues: (1) project page link is blank; (2) title emphasizes 'Multi-Scale Local' but speedup primarily from multi-scale (locality improves upon rejection baseline); (3) overclaimed bridging 'efficiency and fidelity gap' given FID degradation

Missing critical comparisons: no self-speculative decoding evaluation (could eliminate two-checkpoint bottleneck); limited exploration of alternative upsampler architectures or draft/target ratios beyond 2×/4×

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Tar-1.5B/7B, LlamaGen) and resolutions with multiple metrics (GenEval, DPG-Bench, FID, HPSv2) on MS-COCO 5k
Strong empirical results: up to 5.33× speedup at 1024p substantially outperforms LANTERN (1.45×) while maintaining comparable semantic alignment
Thorough ablation studies (Figure 5) systematically validate each component including upsampler design, probability pooling, local expansion, and parallel decoding
Well-motivated problem: accelerating next-token prediction AR models for unified MLLMs is underexplored despite importance
Clear methodology with reproducible implementation: Algorithm 1 is well-specified, hyperparameters clearly documented, comprehensive supplementary details on training procedures
Effective use of spatial locality: local expansion mechanism (Eq. 6-7) is intuitive, well-justified empirically, and ablations confirm necessity
Practical latency analysis (Figure 7) provides useful component-wise breakdown showing minimal overhead from proposed mechanism
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (multi-scale AR models, LANTERN's relaxed acceptance criteria, ZipAR's locality-aware decoding) without introducing fundamentally new concepts; local expansion is intuitive but not a deep technical contribution

Significant practical constraints under-addressed: requires dual model checkpoints increasing memory overhead, effectiveness depends on drafter-verifier distributional alignment (evidenced by weaker LlamaGen results: 1.40× vs 1.94× for Tar-1.5B at 512p), and model-specific training of up/down-samplers (150k steps)

Non-negligible quality degradation at higher resolutions: FID drops 1.3-3.3 points at 1024p, GenEval drops 0.3-2.3 points, HPSv2 drops 0.3-1.0 points consistently; quality-speed tradeoff less favorable than initially apparent

Incomplete comparison to simpler baseline: ZipAR achieves 3.65× speedup at 1024p with minimal quality loss and no training required; MULO-SD's 3.90-5.33× comes with quality degradation and training overhead; Figure 8 shows ZipAR often dominates Pareto front on perceptual quality

Limited theoretical justification: why local expansion preserves quality lacks formalization; no theoretical bounds on acceptance rates or speedup; connection between spatial locality in attention and local expansion effectiveness remains informal

Evaluation scope limitations: only MS-COCO validation, latency on A100 batch-size 1 (unclear scaling), missing comparisons to other acceleration methods (quantization, distillation); no analysis of failure modes

Hyperparameter sensitivity under-explored: method introduces multiple hyperparameters (τ, k, δ, l); τ requires sweeping to match LANTERN; optimal l=3 determined only for 512p, assumed to generalize to 1024p due to computational constraints rather than principled justification

LANTERN baseline credibility issue: supplementary reveals significant underperformance of LANTERN on Tar vs. LlamaGen (Top-1 accuracy 0.12 vs 0.38), attributed to Tar being 'stronger' but making baseline comparison less clean and raising implementation fidelity questions

Practical limitations acknowledged but not solved: self-speculative decoding suggested as remedy for dual-checkpoint requirement but not explored; no experiments on distributional mismatch between drafter and verifier

Presentation issues: notational inconsistency (τ for both temperature and acceptance threshold), key details relegated to supplementary (Eq. 10), missing project page URL, no error bars or confidence intervals on metrics
